subject: Genetics
title: The Dark Matter of the Genome
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Dark Matter of the Genome usable.

hook.text: Only 1.5% of your genome codes for proteins. The other 98.5% was called 'junk DNA.' It wasn't junk at all.

buildup.text: For decades, scientists ignored non-coding DNA. If it didn't make proteins, it seemed useless. A blind spot.

discovery.text: The ENCODE project found 80% of the genome has biochemical function: regulation, structure, RNA production.

twist.text: Many disease-linked mutations sit in non-coding regions. The 'junk' controls when and where genes activate.

climax.text: Non-coding DNA is like software code comments that turn out to be critical instructions. Ignoring it was the error.

punchline.text: The 'junk' runs the show. We just didn't know yet.

quiz.question: What percentage of the genome codes for proteins?
